166: ## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA
167: 
168: - **SC-001**: A weak model that opens a scaffold sees one imperative action and one good and one weak example for every section it must fill.
169: - **SC-002**: A filled section leaves no residue that the placeholder gate counts as an unfilled placeholder.
170: - **SC-003**: A maintainer who edits one example anchor can detect the drift with one command that prints one line per failure.

176: ## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES
177: 
178: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |
179: |------|------|--------|------------|
180: | Dependency | Phase 003 keeps its conversion rule and stamp | Every locator is stale | Each row in `plan.md` gives the heading, which phase 003 does not change, so the insert point survives either form |
181: | Dependency | The template contract keeps the required and optional anchor lists | The drift guard reports false drift | The guard calls the contract, so it inherits any change instead of hard-coding a list |
182: | Risk | A lane edits a file another lane owns | Two writers on one file | The three lanes own disjoint paths and the conductor checks `git status` after each lane |
183: | Risk | The fill text is too long for a table cell and breaks the template | A scaffold renders broken | Every line is one physical line and the fill test renders all 16 documents |
184: | Risk | A snapshot regeneration hides a real regression | A broken render passes | The fill test and the anchor count run separately from the snapshot diff, and the frontier review reads the rendered sections |
185: <!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->
186: 
187: ---
188: 
189: 
190: ## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
191: 
192: ### Performance
193: - **NFR-P01**: The 16 renders in the fill test finish under 60 seconds on the build worktree.
194: 
195: ### Security
196: - **NFR-S01**: No brief carries a credential, token or key. Workers inherit provider login from the environment only.
197: 
198: ### Reliability
199: - **NFR-R01**: The drift guard is read-only and exits 1 on any drift, so a second run on the same tree prints the same lines.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 8. EDGE CASES
204: 
205: ### Data Boundaries
206: - Empty input: a template with no `## ` heading fails the fill test with a named message rather than passing silently.
207: - Maximum length: a fill line that would exceed 400 characters is shortened at authoring time. The test does not enforce a length, the review does.
208: 
209: ### Error Scenarios
210: - External service failure: a provider error stops the lane dispatch. The conductor records it and retries once after 10 minutes, then stops the phase.
211: - Phase 003 not closed: the token form is absent, but the heading locator still works. The conductor records the deviation and continues with the heading form.
212: - A section that exists only at one level: the fill line sits inside the same gate as the heading, so it renders only at that level.
213: 
214: ---
215: 
216: ## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT
217: 
218: | Dimension | Score | Triggers |
219: |-----------|-------|----------|
220: | Scope | 14/25 | Files: 38 changed, 0 external systems |
221: | Risk | 6/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: N |
222: | Research | 12/20 | Seven anchor repairs, 14 example diffs, one renderer contract |
223: | Multi-Agent | 12/15 | Workstreams: 3 edit lanes and 1 conductor |
224: | Coordination | 8/15 | Dependencies: phase 003 only |
225: | **Total** | **52/100** | **Level 3** |
226: 
227: ---
228: 
229: ## 10. RISK MATRIX
230: 
231: | Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
232: |---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|
233: | R-001 | Phase 003 changes a heading, not only a hint | M | L | Every row names a heading, and T001 confirms the headings on the post-003 tree |
234: | R-002 | A lane writes a file another lane owns | H | L | Disjoint paths, and the conductor checks `git status` after each lane |
235: | R-003 | The drift guard treats an optional section as drift | M | M | The guard reads the contract, which marks optional anchors |
236: | R-004 | The snapshot diff hides a visible render error | M | L | The fill test and the frontier review read the rendered sections |
237: | R-005 | A weak model copies the weak example | H | L | The weak example carries a `WEAK:` label and the instruction names the failure |
238: 
239: ---
240: 
241: ## 11. USER STORIES
242: 
243: ### US-001: A section that tells the model what to write (Priority: P0)
244: 
245: **As a** DeepSeek V4.1 Flash worker, **I want** one imperative instruction and one good and one weak example under each heading, **so that** I copy a standard instead of inventing one.
246: 
247: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
248: 
249: ---
250: 
251: ### US-002: A guard that catches example drift (Priority: P0)
252: 
253: **As a** maintainer, **I want** one read-only command that names every example whose anchors differ from its template, **so that** a template edit cannot silently leave the examples stale.
254: 
255: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
256: 
257: ---
258: 
259: <!-- ANCHOR:questions -->
260: ## 12. OPEN QUESTIONS
261: 
262: - None that block this phase. Every choice it needs is frozen in `goal.md` section 1.
263: - Deferred: should a later gate reject a leftover fill comment in a filled document. The comment is not a placeholder today, so this phase leaves the decision to phase 005.
264: <!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->

271: - **Task Breakdown**: See `tasks.md`
272: - **Verification Checklist**: See `tasks.md`
273: - **Decision Records**: See `plan.md` section L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD

57: ## 3. ARCHITECTURE
58: 
59: ### Pattern
60: Three disjoint edit lanes, then one conductor-owned golden regeneration and one gate run.
61: 
62: ### Facts read from the tree while this plan was written
63: 
64: Every fact below came from a read-only command or a file read. The command is repeated so the conductor can confirm it on the post-003 tree.

The Level 1 lists are the six to seven names in the phase brief |

90: ### The fill line format (frozen)
91: 
92: One physical line, placed immediately below the section heading.
93: 
94: ```text
95: <!-- FILL: <instruction> GOOD: <good example> WEAK: <weak example> -->
96: ```
97: 
98: When the table below has `-` in both the Good and the Weak cell, the line is:
99: 
100: ```text
101: <!-- FILL: <instruction> -->
102: ```
103: 
104: Rules for the text inside the line:
105: - The instruction is one imperative sentence and ends with a period.
106: - No cell contains `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:`, `[NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:`, `-->`, `;` or an em dash. A short priority mark such as `[P0]` is allowed because it is not a token.
107: - The line is never wrapped. It is one line in the template source.
108: - The good example is concrete and short. The weak example is the failure a weak model produces: vague, generic or a restatement of the heading.
109: - The model deletes the line when it fills the section. A line left behind is not a placeholder, so it never fails the gate.

90: ### The fill line format (frozen)
91: 
92: One physical line, placed immediately below the section heading.
93: 
94: ```text
95: <!-- FILL: <instruction> GOOD: <good example> WEAK: <weak example> -->
96: ```
97: 
98: When the table below has `-` in both the Good and the Weak cell, the line is:
99: 
100: ```text
101: <!-- FILL: <instruction> -->
102: ```
103: 
104: Rules for the text inside the line:
105: - The instruction is one imperative sentence and ends with a period.
106: - No cell contains `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:`, `[NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:`, `-->`, `;` or an em dash. A short priority mark such as `[P0]` is allowed because it is not a token.
107: - The line is never wrapped. It is one line in the template source.
108: - The good example is concrete and short. The weak example is the failure a weak model produces: vague, generic or a restatement of the heading.
109: - The model deletes the line when it fills the section. A line left behind is not a placeholder, so it never fails the gate.

891: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
892: 
893: ### ADR-001: Put the guidance in an HTML comment below the heading
894: 
895: **Status**: Accepted
896: 
897: **Context**: The guidance must not trip phase 003's token gate, must work for a prose paragraph, a table cell and a checklist item, and must not break the header comparison in `template-structure.js`.
898: 
899: **Decision**: Each section carries one ordinary HTML comment on its own line, immediately below the heading: `<!-- FILL: ... -->`. The existing value tokens stay where they are and remain field-level prompts.
900: 
901: **Consequences**:
902: - The gate ignores the line because it holds no token syntax.
903: - The line renders into the scaffold but is invisible on the rendered page.
904: - A model that leaves the line behind leaves a harmless comment, not an unfilled placeholder.
905: 
906: **Alternatives Rejected**:
907: - Inside the token: a long instruction inside a table cell breaks the table, and a checklist item cannot hold it.
908: - On the heading line: `template-structure.js` compares heading text, so a comment in the heading would make every filled document differ from its contract.
909: - A separate guide file: a weak model fills the section in front of it and does not follow a pointer to a second file.
910: 
911: ### ADR-002: One fill line per section, not per hint
912: 
913: **Status**: Accepted
914: 
915: **Context**: The five templates phase 003 converts hold 214 hints after its conversion, and the four core templates hold 70 heading rows. One line per hint would repeat the same instruction many times and make the plan unreadable.
916: 
917: **Decision**: One line per `## ` section. It names the one action for the section. The tokens inside the section stay as field-level prompts.
918: 
919: **Consequences**:
920: - The plan is bounded and the model reads one instruction per section.
921: - A section with eight tokens still has one governing instruction.
922: 
923: **Alternatives Rejected**:
924: - Per-token guidance: repetitive, and it hides the section-level action in a crowd of field prompts.
925: 
926: ### ADR-003: Delegate anchor comparison to the template contract
927: 
928: **Status**: Accepted
929: 
930: **Context**: A hand-rolled anchor set comparison would duplicate the contract and drift from the validator.
931: 
932: **Decision**: `check-example-drift.sh` calls `node runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js compare <level> <doc> <example> anchors` and fails on any `missing_anchor` or `extra_anchor` line.
933: 
934: **Consequences**:
935: - The guard and the validator read one source of truth.
936: - The guard inherits the contract's dynamic ADR handling for `decision-record.md`.
937: 
938: **Alternatives Rejected**:
939: - A bash set difference: it would need its own copy of the required and optional lists.
940: 
941: ### ADR-004: Examples satisfy required anchors and add no extra anchor
942: 
943: **Status**: Accepted
944: 
945: **Context**: The contract marks some anchors optional, and an example may legitimately omit an optional section. Full equality would force optional sections into every example and would fight the dynamic ADR anchors.
946: 
947: **Decision**: An example must carry every required anchor and no anchor outside the template's allowed set. Optional anchors may be absent.
948: 
949: **Consequences**:
950: - The alignment table is 14 files, not 24.
951: - A missing optional section is not drift.
952: 
953: **Alternatives Rejected**:
954: - Full set equality: it would force `affected-surfaces` and the L3+ workstream sections into every example.
955: 
956: ### ADR-005: Regenerate the golden snapshots once, by the conductor
957: 
958: **Status**: Accepted
959: 
960: **Context**: The golden test stores 25 renders. Two lanes edit templates, and one snapshot file cannot take two writers.
961: 
962: **Decision**: Lanes A and B finish first. The conductor runs `npx vitest run runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts -u` once, then reruns without `-u`.
963: 
964: **Consequences**:
965: - One snapshot diff covers every template change.
966: - No lane writes the snapshot file.
967: - A mutation run proves the test notices a render change: T010 inserts one Level 1-only line, expects `Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)` and exit 1, restores the backup and reruns to `Tests  12 passed (12)`.
968: 
969: **Alternatives Rejected**:
970: - Each lane updates the snapshots: two lanes would write one file, which breaks the frozen lane rule.
971: 
972: ### ADR-006: Optional sections may be deleted, required sections get N/A
973: 
974: **Status**: Accepted
975: 
976: **Context**: A weak model invents a feature flag, an OWASP review and an uptime target for a documentation packet. The contract decides which sections may disappear.
977: 
978: **Decision**: The fill line for an optional section says either `N/A` with one reason or delete the section. The fill line for a required section says `N/A` with one reason and never says delete.
979: 
980: **Consequences**:
981: - A packet with no service stops inventing an uptime target.
982: - A Level 3+ compliance checkpoint stays present because the contract requires it.
983: 
984: **Alternatives Rejected**:
985: - Remove the generic sections from the templates: the Level 3+ contract requires three of them.
986:

891: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
892: 
893: ### ADR-001: Put the guidance in an HTML comment below the heading
894: 
895: **Status**: Accepted
896: 
897: **Context**: The guidance must not trip phase 003's token gate, must work for a prose paragraph, a table cell and a checklist item, and must not break the header comparison in `template-structure.js`.
898: 
899: **Decision**: Each section carries one ordinary HTML comment on its own line, immediately below the heading: `<!-- FILL: ... -->`. The existing value tokens stay where they are and remain field-level prompts.
900: 
901: **Consequences**:
902: - The gate ignores the line because it holds no token syntax.
903: - The line renders into the scaffold but is invisible on the rendered page.
904: - A model that leaves the line behind leaves a harmless comment, not an unfilled placeholder.
905: 
906: **Alternatives Rejected**:
907: - Inside the token: a long instruction inside a table cell breaks the table, and a checklist item cannot hold it.
908: - On the heading line: `template-structure.js` compares heading text, so a comment in the heading would make every filled document differ from its contract.
909: - A separate guide file: a weak model fills the section in front of it and does not follow a pointer to a second file.
910: 
911: ### ADR-002: One fill line per section, not per hint
912: 
913: **Status**: Accepted
914: 
915: **Context**: The five templates phase 003 converts hold 214 hints after its conversion, and the four core templates hold 70 heading rows. One line per hint would repeat the same instruction many times and make the plan unreadable.
916: 
917: **Decision**: One line per `## ` section. It names the one action for the section. The tokens inside the section stay as field-level prompts.
918: 
919: **Consequences**:
920: - The plan is bounded and the model reads one instruction per section.
921: - A section with eight tokens still has one governing instruction.
922: 
923: **Alternatives Rejected**:
924: - Per-token guidance: repetitive, and it hides the section-level action in a crowd of field prompts.
925: 
926: ### ADR-003: Delegate anchor comparison to the template contract
927: 
928: **Status**: Accepted
929: 
930: **Context**: A hand-rolled anchor set comparison would duplicate the contract and drift from the validator.
931: 
932: **Decision**: `check-example-drift.sh` calls `node runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js compare <level> <doc> <example> anchors` and fails on any `missing_anchor` or `extra_anchor` line.
933: 
934: **Consequences**:
935: - The guard and the validator read one source of truth.
936: - The guard inherits the contract's dynamic ADR handling for `decision-record.md`.
937: 
938: **Alternatives Rejected**:
939: - A bash set difference: it would need its own copy of the required and optional lists.
940: 
941: ### ADR-004: Examples satisfy required anchors and add no extra anchor
942: 
943: **Status**: Accepted
944: 
945: **Context**: The contract marks some anchors optional, and an example may legitimately omit an optional section. Full equality would force optional sections into every example and would fight the dynamic ADR anchors.
946: 
947: **Decision**: An example must carry every required anchor and no anchor outside the template's allowed set. Optional anchors may be absent.
948: 
949: **Consequences**:
950: - The alignment table is 14 files, not 24.
951: - A missing optional section is not drift.
952: 
953: **Alternatives Rejected**:
954: - Full set equality: it would force `affected-surfaces` and the L3+ workstream sections into every example.
955: 
956: ### ADR-005: Regenerate the golden snapshots once, by the conductor
957: 
958: **Status**: Accepted
959: 
960: **Context**: The golden test stores 25 renders. Two lanes edit templates, and one snapshot file cannot take two writers.
961: 
962: **Decision**: Lanes A and B finish first. The conductor runs `npx vitest run runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts -u` once, then reruns without `-u`.
963: 
964: **Consequences**:
965: - One snapshot diff covers every template change.
966: - No lane writes the snapshot file.
967: - A mutation run proves the test notices a render change: T010 inserts one Level 1-only line, expects `Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)` and exit 1, restores the backup and reruns to `Tests  12 passed (12)`.
968: 
969: **Alternatives Rejected**:
970: - Each lane updates the snapshots: two lanes would write one file, which breaks the frozen lane rule.
971: 
972: ### ADR-006: Optional sections may be deleted, required sections get N/A
973: 
974: **Status**: Accepted
975: 
976: **Context**: A weak model invents a feature flag, an OWASP review and an uptime target for a documentation packet. The contract decides which sections may disappear.
977: 
978: **Decision**: The fill line for an optional section says either `N/A` with one reason or delete the section. The fill line for a required section says `N/A` with one reason and never says delete.
979: 
980: **Consequences**:
981: - A packet with no service stops inventing an uptime target.
982: - A Level 3+ compliance checkpoint stays present because the contract requires it.
983: 
984: **Alternatives Rejected**:
985: - Remove the generic sections from the templates: the Level 3+ contract requires three of them.

104:   }

107:     level="${dir##*/level-}"

109:       name="$(basename "$example")"
110:       desc="$(awk '/^description:/{sub(/^description:[[:space:]]*/,""); print; exit}' "$example")"

112:       bare="${bare#\"}"
113:       [[ "$bare" == *"-->"* ]] && fail "$example" "description holds an HTML comment tail"
114:       [[ "$bare" == [[:lower:]]* ]] && fail "$example" "description starts lowercase"
115:       [[ "$bare" == *. ]] || fail "$example" "description does not end with a period"
